newsitem.title: UK: EURO OIL SWAPS SLIP, MOGAS DOWN $5 AFTER SQUEEZE.
newsitem.headline: EURO OIL SWAPS SLIP, MOGAS DOWN $5 AFTER SQUEEZE.

text.p: European oil swaps slipped again on Friday as gasoline extended a three day plunge by dropping a further $13 a tonne on physical barges and $5 on August swaps.
Dealers said a squeeze by Wall Street trader Morgan Stanley that lifted prices by some $25 a tonne over the past week appeared to have ended.
August swaps were heard traded at $211 compared to a peak of $223.50 on Tuesday while September traded three times at $194.
Physical barges traded at $216 and then $220 but some dealers expected further falls in the wake of the summer driving season.
Naphtha also fell but less sharply as Asian swaps sank further into contango with August dipping $3 to $191.50 and September around $186.25 by lunchtime.
Gas oil was little changed with premiums for EN590 holding around $6 a tonne above the IPE for September and $9.50 above for the fourth quarter.
Crack spreads fell around 15 cents a barrel to $4.50 for the fourth and first quarters.
Heavy fuel was unchanged although bids were difficult to find by lunchtime. August traded at $94.50 with September 50 cents higher and the fourth quarter around $96.75.

Brent crude CFDs slipped and sank into deeper contango. Next week's dates fell five cents to 38 cents under October while the following two weeks were down three cents to 34 cents under and 33 cents under respectively.
